headline: European soccer votes to boycott the World Cup

sources.title: UEFA members agree FIFA boycott if World Cup plans pursued
UEFA vows World Cup boycott as Concacaf, AFC reject FIFA private equity plan
UEFA threatens World Cup boycott over FIFA private equity plan
European nations vow to boycott World Cup over FIFA's private equity plan (video, Associated Press)

chunks.text: All 55 European soccer [[associations]] voted on July 30 to [[boycott]] every FIFA competition if FIFA {{goes ahead with}} a plan to sell part of the World Cup to private [[investors]]. Their statement was [[blunt]]. No European national team will {{take part in}} any FIFA competition [[for as long as]] the plan [[is alive]]. It is the sharpest [[split]] between European soccer and the world [[governing body]] [[in living memory]].

verbs.wrong: To agree to a plan without acting
verbs.why: Go ahead with means to continue a plan even when other people have doubts or complaints. Organizers decided to go ahead with the event despite strong opposition.
Take part in means to join an activity or event together with other people. Every national team was asked whether it would take part in the tournament.

chunks.text: The plan was {{put forward}} by FIFA president Gianni Infantino. It would move the World Cup and other [[tournaments]] into a new company worth about 20 billion dollars. FIFA would {{hold on to}} a [[majority]] of that company and {{sell off}} a [[minority]] [[share]], [[up to]] 20 percent, to raise [[as much as]] 4.2 billion dollars. The investor group that has {{lined up}} to lead the purchase is an American [[venture capital]] firm founded by Joshua Kushner, whose brother is married to the daughter of the American president. Each of FIFA's 211 [[member]] associations was offered 20 million dollars and asked to reply by [[the middle of]] September.

verbs.correct: To suggest an idea to others
verbs.why: Put forward means to formally suggest an idea or plan for others to consider. A leader put forward a proposal that many members strongly opposed.
Hold on to means to keep control of something rather than transferring it to someone else. The organization wanted to hold on to most of the ownership for itself.

verbs.wrong: To divide a company in two
verbs.why: Sell off means to sell part of what you own, often to raise money quickly. A company might sell off a small share of itself to outside investors.

verbs.wrong: To be chosen by a vote
verbs.why: Line up means to arrange or prepare something before it is officially needed. Investors had already lined up a deal before the public even heard about it.

chunks.text: European officials say the money is not the point. A World Cup, they argue, is held for the countries that play in it, and is therefore not FIFA's to sell. Their earlier statement said the plan [[crossed a line]] that soccer's governing [[institutions]] should never cross, and that the soul and [[governance]] of soccer are not [[assets]] to trade. The Asian [[confederation]] called [[the lack of]] [[consultation]] totally [[unacceptable]]. The confederation covering North and Central America also {{came out against}} the plan. Infantino has since {{played down}} the plan, calling it a [[proposal]] [[rather than]] a decision.

verbs.wrong: To refuse to take a side
verbs.why: Come out against means to state publicly that you oppose a plan or a decision. Several major organizations quickly came out against the proposal.
Play down means to describe something as less serious or significant than it actually is. Leaders sometimes play down criticism to avoid making a conflict worse.

chunks.text: Nothing can pass without a vote of all 211 members, and 55 of them have now said they will {{walk away}} instead. The next FIFA tournament is the Women's Under 20 World Cup in Poland, which {{kicks off}} on September 5. If the plan is still alive [[by then]], the boycott begins with a [[youth]] tournament rather than with the World Cup itself.

verbs.why: Walk away means to leave a situation completely, often as a form of protest. Members threatened to walk away from every competition run by the organization.
Kick off means an event officially begins, especially a competition or tournament. The next big tournament kicks off in just a few weeks.

mainIdea.s: All 55 European soccer associations voted to boycott FIFA over its World Cup sale plan. If the plan is still alive by September, the boycott will start with a youth tournament in Poland.
mainIdea.why: The vote covers every FIFA competition. If the plan continues, the boycott starts with the Women's Under 20 World Cup in Poland in September.

mainIdea.s: The vote among Europe's national teams supports a boycott of only the World Cup, not other FIFA events. All 211 of FIFA's member associations must still decide on the plan before mid-September.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the article says the boycott covers every FIFA competition, not just the World Cup itself.

mainIdea.s: FIFA's member associations are separately reviewing ticket prices for the next World Cup in North America. That review should end with a new pricing plan before the tournament begins next summer.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a boycott threat over FIFA's investment plan, not about ticket prices or a new pricing plan.
